elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no affiliate-assignment exception; an assignment to an affiliate remains subject to the other party's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: Although merger-related assignments are generally permitted without consent upon notice, consent is required if the transaction involves a direct competitor of Vendor.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: Although acquisition-related assignments are generally permitted without consent upon notice, consent is required if the transaction involves a direct competitor of Vendor.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: Although qualifying asset-sale assignments are generally permitted without consent upon notice, consent is required if the transaction involves a direct competitor of Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Vendor may assign without Customer consent in connection with Vendor's merger or acquisition or a qualifying asset sale, unless the transaction involves a direct competitor of Customer.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The opening consent requirement is expressly qualified by “which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.”

elements.element: Vendor may never assign the Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause requires Customer consent for an assignment involving a direct competitor of Customer but does not prohibit that assignment absolutely.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right upon Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause grants no termination right to Vendor based on Customer's merger, acquisition, asset sale, or other change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor without Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: The successor-transaction exception is not unconditional: Vendor consent is required when the transaction involves a direct competitor of Vendor.

elements.element: Customer must give Vendor written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: Customer's merger-, acquisition-, and qualifying asset-sale assignments are expressly conditioned on written notice to Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement to a successor without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The successor-transaction exception is not unconditional: Customer consent is required when the transaction involves a direct competitor of Customer.

elements.element: Vendor must give Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: Vendor's merger-, acquisition-, and qualifying asset-sale assignments are expressly conditioned on written notice to Customer.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than successor assignments require Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence requires Vendor's prior written consent, subject to the stated successor-transaction exception.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Customer assignment other than a successor assignment.
elements.evidence: The opening consent requirement is expressly qualified by “which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.”

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than successor assignments require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence requires Customer's prior written consent, subject to the stated successor-transaction exception.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment other than a successor assignment.
elements.evidence: The opening consent requirement is expressly qualified by “which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.”

result.reason: The redline adds the mutual reasonableness qualifier and written-notice mechanic, but the retained direct-competitor consent exception prevents either party from having the fallback's notice-only right to assign to all successors. It also falls short of the preferred position because there is no affiliate exception for Customer, Vendor retains consent-free successor-assignment rights in some cases, and Vendor assignments to Customer competitors are consent-based rather than absolutely prohibited. The clause is otherwise coherent and introduces no contradiction, but it does not reach a complete preferred or fallback level.
